reason: The cited evidence shows that annealing improves adhesion and corrosion resistance in NaCl, but provides no data on simultaneous wear-corrosion, oxide layer formation, or the effect of grain size/texture optimization on tribocorrosion. The key mechanistic premises linking nanostructure to a protective oxide under combined wear and corrosion are unsupported.
premises: Annealing CuMoTaWV films can optimize grain size and phase texture without deleterious phase segregation
Optimized nanostructure promotes formation of a stable, adherent passivating oxide layer during simultaneous wear and corrosion
This enhanced oxide layer reduces both friction/wear and corrosion rates compared to the as-deposited state
Over-annealing causes excessive grain coarsening or phase segregation that diminishes protective oxide formation
